<reason>PRO won a close, high-clash debate by keeping a live middle path: high-need roles can still be monitored with a yes and purpose limits, while CON’s default camera-in-the-home is the dragnet the motion exists to block. CON was sharper on mechanics (notice-plus-office is not “refuse and stay remote,” logs do not prove who sat in the chair, and the dual lock can hobble a real presence check), but PRO’s kitchen-table frame, teller-versus-copywriter distinction, and closing recast of A4.3 as face-matching plus durable automated punishment made the ballot easier. CON never showed why output-verified roles must accept that package or lose remote work; PRO never fully killed firm flight from remote, but did not need to once the modest check looked invasive.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO’s close on A4.3: the supposedly modest chair-check required matching, long-lived records, and flags without a human queue, turning CON’s verification story into the bedroom dragnet.</best_rebuttal>
